name: Corner Descent Is Exact in the Cut-Vertex Obstruction Branch
statement: Let an ample pc-minimal obstruction with cut vertex be the one-point amalgam $X=A_1\vee A_2$ at root $a$. For any nonroot corner $x$ of one factor, $X\setminus\{x\}$ is again a pc-minimal obstruction exactly when the rooted pair $(A_i\setminus\{x\},a)$ remains a rooted factor. Consequently a cornered obstruction in this branch is terminal under obstruction-preserving corner deletion exactly when one rooted factor has a nonroot corner but none of its nonroot corner deletions remains a rooted factor.
proof: The corners of the amalgam are exactly the nonroot corners of its two factors: the root has incident directions in both blocks without the mixed square. Deleting such a corner preserves ampleness and the cut vertex. The cut-vertex classification then makes obstruction status equivalent to the rooted-factor conditions on the changed branch; failure to peel to the root is automatic, since otherwise prefixing the deleted corner would root-peel the original factor. For terminality, one direction reads this criterion inside a terminal obstruction. Conversely, glue a rooted factor with the stated deletion property to a known rooted factor whose only corner is its root; every corner then belongs to the first branch and every deletion fails the criterion.
